clue.text: Treatment for mug having to confront wild animals

parts.note: to confront someone is to face them
a pack is a group of wild animals such as wolves

explanation.surface: Someone with an ugly mug is ordered to go and face down a horde of beasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is slang for the face, so the definition is a beauty treatment, not a cure for a cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A face pack is a cosmetic paste spread over the skin, and mug is slang for the face.

clue.text: Supporter abandoning king, his manoeuvres being diabolical

indicators.note: a supporter abandoning the king means the letter for king leaves that word

parts.note: a friend is a supporter
R is short for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: manoeuvres says the letters of the little word his are moved about

explanation.surface: A loyal backer deserts the monarch, whose wicked schemes are plain to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes R out of FRIEND to leave FIEND; 'manoeuvres' turns HIS into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiendish behaviour is devilishly cruel, the way a demon would act.

clue.text: Rank outsiders in constituency supporting centre, we hear

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath the other one
we hear says the word for centre is to be taken by how it is spoken

parts.note: a kernel is the centre of a nut or of an issue

indicators.note: the outsiders in a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A no-hoper candidate from the fringes of a seat backs a centrist party, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rank outsiders' reads as a racing phrase, but Rank is the definition; 'we hear' works on the word for centre, and in a down clue 'supporting' puts the outer letters underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A colonelcy is the military rank or office held by a colonel.

clue.text: Creature taking gold from 'first mortal woman

indicators.note: taking gold from the woman means those letters are removed from her name

parts.note: in Greek myth Pandora was the first mortal woman, made by the gods
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: An animal steals gold from Eve, or her Greek equivalent.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking OR out of PANDORA leaves PANDA.
explanation.definitionFit: A panda is a bear-like animal of China, so it is one kind of creature.

clue.text: Where Persians may be allowed to board

definitions.text: Where Persians may be allowed to board

parts.words: Where Persians may be allowed to board
parts.note: Persians here are long-haired cats, and to board is to lodge for a fee while the owners are away

explanation.surface: Iranian travellers are told where they may get on a ship or plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The reader thinks of people from Persia boarding transport; in fact they are cats being boarded at a lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattery is a place where cats are housed and looked after for a fee.

clue.text: Man is one, regardless of what Donne thought

definitions.text: Man is one, regardless of what Donne thought

parts.words: Man is one, regardless of what Donne thought
parts.note: the Isle of Man is a piece of land in the sea, though John Donne wrote that no man is one

explanation.surface: A thinker argues with the poet John Donne about human nature.
explanation.walkthrough: Donne's famous line says no man stands alone; read Man as the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea, and the statement becomes true.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is surrounded by water, which makes it a piece of land of that kind.

clue.text: In life, perhaps, one reveals power of perception

indicators.note: In at the front says one letter goes inside the word for a prison term

parts.note: a life term is one kind of prison sentence, hence perhaps
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone discovers what it is to be aware at all, in the course of living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'life' is a prison term here: put I inside SENTENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and be aware, the ability to perceive things.

clue.text: Articles about individual male's inner personality

indicators.note: about means the articles wrap round the next two pieces

parts.note: AN and A are both indefinite articles
I, the single person, stands for an individual
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Magazine pieces discuss a particular man's inner self.
explanation.walkthrough: AN and A wrap round I and M. ANIMA is Jung's word for the feminine inner side of a man.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jung's psychology the anima is the inner self, especially a man's unconscious feminine side.

clue.text: Model with little work becoming shapeless lump.

parts.note: a doll is a small model of a person
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A fashion model who barely works out ends up out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: OP, short for opus, is a 'little work'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dollop is a soft, formless blob of something, such as cream or mashed potato.

clue.text: Educational publication with staff all over county

indicators.note: all over says the whole run of letters is turned over, last to first

parts.note: TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a UK newspaper for teachers
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: A teachers' paper and its staff are spread right across the shire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over' turns TESROD backwards. DORSET is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorset is a county on the south coast of England.

clue.text: Lady of the lake rejecting little heroine, English

indicators.note: rejecting means the heroine's name is sent back, letters reversed

parts.note: Little Nell is the heroine of Dickens's The Old Curiosity Shop

explanation.surface: A lady of the lake turns down a part as a tiny English heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejecting' reverses Dickens's heroine. Ellen Douglas is the heroine of Walter Scott's poem The Lady of the Lake, so 'lake' is no clue to water.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scott's poem The Lady of the Lake, the title lady is Ellen Douglas.

clue.text: Small bird finally caught by large one

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of caught is used

parts.note: the hornbill is a large bird, one of the kind just named

explanation.surface: A little bird is at last snatched by a much bigger one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' stands for 'bird' again: the large bird is the HORNBILL, and T is the last letter of caught.
explanation.definitionFit: Thornbills are small Australian songbirds, tiny warblers.

clue.text: Smelly substance clinging to a Welshman's overalls

parts.note: dung is animal droppings, a smelly substance
Rees is a typical Welsh name

explanation.surface: A Welsh farmer's work clothes are caked with manure.
explanation.walkthrough: DUNG, then A, then REES. Rees is a common Welsh surname used in crosswords for a Welshman.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are hard-wearing trousers with a bib, a kind of work overalls.

clue.text: Single party taking a husband in northern state

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, so single

indicators.note: the party taking these letters means they go inside it

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A lone partygoer turns up with a husband in a state up north.
explanation.walkthrough: DO takes A and H inside it, after I. IDAHO is a US state on the Canadian border.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a US state in the north-west, bordering Canada.

clue.text: Continuously taking sun in indolent manner

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
to do something idly is to do it in an indolent manner

explanation.surface: Someone lazily soaks up the sun all day long.
explanation.walkthrough: SOL, then IDLY. 'Continuously' fits in the sense of 'without a break'.
explanation.definitionFit: Working solidly means working without a break, steadily and without interruption.

clue.text: Rum brand like this? It should be!

definitions.text: Rum brand like this? It should be!

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd, so these two words come out in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A drinker hopes a brand of rum would be pleasant to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink, but it is the anagram signal on BRAND LIKE. The whole clue is also the definition: a rum brand should be fit to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drinkable is fit to be drunk, which is what any rum on sale should be.

clue.text: Fish found way back inside Arctic region

indicators.note: inside means the reversed road goes into the fish

parts.note: tuna is a fish

indicators.note: back says the letters for way are turned round

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A fish turns up on the way back into the frozen north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the road abbreviation before 'inside' puts it into the fish; 'way' as RD is a common crossword shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is the vast treeless plain of the Arctic, with frozen subsoil.

clue.text: Entertainment for which a box is reserved

definitions.text: Entertainment for which a box is reserved

parts.words: Entertainment for which a box is reserved
parts.note: in a theatre a box is booked ahead, but here the box is the case the show itself is carried and watched in

explanation.surface: A theatre keeps a private box booked for a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A theatre box springs to mind, but the box is the show: a raree show was a peep show carried round in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A raree show was a street peep show, pictures viewed through a hole in a portable box.

clue.text: Eastern girl outside is state's first envoy

indicators.note: the girl is outside, so her name goes round the next letters

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name

indicators.note: first means only the first letter of state's is used

explanation.surface: A girl from the East is the nation's leading diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl's name is split after its first letter by 'outside', taking in IS and the first letter of 'state's'; 'Eastern' supplies only its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An emissary is a person sent on a mission as a representative, the same job as a diplomatic messenger.

clue.text: One identifies writer through exaggerated story

parts.note: by means through, as in by means of
a line is a tall story, as in to shoot a line

explanation.surface: A tall tale gives away who wrote it.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'shoot a line' is to boast, so a line is an exaggerated story.
explanation.definitionFit: A byline is the line naming the author at the top of a newspaper article.

clue.text: Give off, being English, cross, and having fit

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross
hale means fit and healthy

explanation.surface: An Englishman, angry and having a seizure, lets off steam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' and 'fit' look like anger and a seizure; they are X and HALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to breathe out, sending air or vapour off.

clue.text: More unusual addition to the proposition to be proved

indicators.note: an addition to a word comes after it, joined on at the end
unusual says the letters of More are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A stranger statement gets added to the proposition awaiting proof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More unusual' looks like a comparative, but 'unusual' is the anagram signal on MORE, giving OREM, added to THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A theorem in mathematics is a statement that has to be proved from axioms.

clue.text: Determining centre and ends of route

indicators.note: the centre of the word Determining contains the letters wanted, its ends dropped

explanation.surface: A traveller works out the middle and the end points of a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in the middle of 'Determining', not its exact centre letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are the end stations of a railway or bus line, the end points of a route.

clue.text: Emotional problem makes us break off conversation

definitions.meaning: a fixation or neurosis that troubles someone
to put the phone down and end a call

explanation.surface: A personal hang-up stops us chatting.
explanation.walkthrough: As a noun it is a neurosis; as a verb it is ending a phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: A hang-up is an emotional inhibition, and to hang up is to end a telephone call.

clue.text: A king accepting overthrow of state, sad to say

indicators.note: accepting means the first two letters take another piece in between them

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: overthrow of means the state's letters are turned upside down, last to first

parts.note: Cal is short for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A king allows his realm to be toppled, unfortunately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrow of' reverses the California abbreviation and 'accepting' lodges it between A and K. Alack is an archaic cry of regret, like alas.
explanation.definitionFit: Alack is an old exclamation of sorrow, meaning unfortunately or alas.

clue.text: Where one may act as protector

definitions.meaning: the stage area in front of the curtain, where actors perform
a garment worn to protect clothes, as in a kitchen

explanation.surface: An actor serves as a guardian.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is the theatre's forestage; the other is a garment tied on to keep clothes clean.
explanation.definitionFit: An apron is the part of a stage in front of the curtain, and also a cover worn over clothes.

clue.text: Robust character of girl performing routine work?

indicators.note: a girl performing routine work is one in harness, so she goes inside that word

parts.note: to be in harness is to be at one's routine daily work
Di is short for Diana, a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman doing her daily chores shows great strength of character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in harness' is an idiom for being at one's daily work, so a girl 'performing routine work' is a girl inside that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardiness is toughness, the quality of being robust and able to endure hardship.

clue.text: Fill with universal drug one doctor introduces

indicators.note: one doctor introduces the other pieces, so those letters come first

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
U is the film certificate for universal viewing
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A medic brings in a drug for everyone, filling patients with it.
explanation.walkthrough: I and MB come first, introducing U (the UK film rating for all audiences) and E (ecstasy).
explanation.definitionFit: To imbue something is to saturate or fill it with a quality or substance.

clue.text: Italian hero worn out by woman?

definitions.meaning: the soldier who led the unification of Italy in the nineteenth century
a loose red blouse worn by women out in public, named after him

explanation.surface: A national hero is exhausted by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worn out' suggests exhausted, but it means worn when out: a Garibaldi is a woman's blouse modelled on his followers' red shirts.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Garibaldi led Italy's unification, and a garibaldi was a loose women's blouse named after his red shirts.

clue.text: Leaves a lot to be desired? Of poor quality, actually

definitions.text: Leaves a lot to be desired? Of poor quality, actually

parts.words: Leaves a lot to be desired? Of poor quality, actually
parts.note: leaves here are tea leaves, and the phrase for something unsatisfying turns out literally true of a cheap grade of tea

explanation.surface: A critic sniffs that something falls short and is in fact shoddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' is a noun, tea leaves: bohea was once the name for the lowest grade of black China tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohea is a black China tea, the name later given to its poorest, last-picked grade.

clue.text: Pawn on board finally taken by queen — that's deliberate

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of board is used

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A chess player moves a pawn deep into the queen's reach on purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: P, ON, the last letter of board, then ER (Elizabeth Regina). 'deliberate' is a verb, not 'on purpose'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ponder is to think something over carefully, weighing it up.

clue.text: Only Jekyll to be found, say, in this' retreat?

indicators.note: say tells us to take the phrase as it would be pronounced

parts.note: if only Dr Jekyll is around, then Mr Hyde is away

explanation.surface: Dr Jekyll alone can be found in this secluded refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: In Stevenson's story Jekyll and Hyde are one man; if only Jekyll is present, 'Hyde away' is spoken just like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideaway is a secret place to escape to, a refuge.
